    Predictions from meta-analytic models

    Source: R/broom-methods.R
    predict.meta_fit.Rd

    Predicted (average) effects with confidence or prediction intervals. For models with moderators, newdata supplies the moderator values; for models without moderators the pooled estimate is returned. Prediction intervals add the between-study variance to the variance of the prediction.

    Usage

    # S3 method for class 'meta_fit'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  interval = c("confidence", "prediction", "none"),
  level = NULL,
  ...
)

    Arguments

    object

    A <meta_fit>.

    newdata

    Optional data frame of moderator values (or, for meta_subgroup() fits, of the grouping variable).

    interval

    "confidence", "prediction" or "none".

    level

    Confidence level. Defaults to the level of the fit.

    ...

    Not used.

    Value

    A tibble with .pred, .se and, unless interval = "none", .pred_lower and .pred_upper. Without newdata, models with moderators return one row per study and models without moderators a single row.

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
fit <- meta_regress(bcg, ~ ablat)
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(ablat = c(10, 50)),
        interval = "prediction")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>     .pred   .se .pred_lower .pred_upper
#>     <dbl> <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 -0.0395 0.187      -0.693       0.614
#> 2 -1.20   0.172      -1.84       -0.566
